coach.nutrition.considerations.title: Highlights
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_prot: High in protein, a key nutrient to repair and strengthen muscle.
Strong protein contribution to support recovery and muscle mass.
High in protein, a macronutrient that also helps with satiety.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_prote: Modest protein contribution; pair it with other sources to complete the meal.
Low in protein, better combined with denser protein foods.
Not a protein standout; it mainly contributes other macronutrients.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_carb: A direct energy source for daily activity and training.
Carbohydrates predominate, the body's main fuel.
Provides carbohydrates to maintain energy and refill glycogen.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_carbs: Very low in carbohydrates, with a minimal impact on energy stores.
Reduced carbohydrate content, useful for managing daily energy load.
Barely contributes carbs, so it fits easily into lower-carb plans.
coach.nutrition.considerations.healthy_f: Contains good-quality fats that support normal body function.
Stands out for its unsaturated fat profile, beneficial for heart health.
A source of healthy fats that also help absorb some vitamins.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_satu: High saturated fat; worth factoring in when planning the rest of the day.
A considerable saturated fat concentration, better eaten in moderation.
Saturated fats make up a high share of its total fat.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_salt: High sodium; consider moderating the portion if you are watching salt.
High salt concentration from processing, curing or seasoning.
Adds a notable amount of sodium to the daily total.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_suga: Contains fast-absorbing sugars that provide immediate energy.
A notable amount of simple sugars; better used at specific times.
High sugar concentration to keep in mind for a balanced intake.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_fibe: High in fiber, a key element for digestion and gut transit.
A high fiber contribution that helps keep you fuller for longer.
Excellent fiber content, supporting a more gradual energy release.
coach.nutrition.considerations.high_calo: High energy density; it packs a lot of energy into a small portion.
A very energy-dense option, useful when calorie needs are high.
High calorie concentration, so portion size should match your goal.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_calor: Very low in calories, useful for adding volume without much energy.
A light option with a low energy contribution, easy to include.
Reduced calorie content, ideal when you want a bigger plate.
coach.nutrition.considerations.micronutr: Stands out for its natural contribution of essential micronutrients.
Provides vitamins and minerals with relevant nutritional value.
A notable micronutrient contribution that complements the food profile.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_salt_: Clean profile: low in added sugars and sodium.
Moderate in salt and simple sugars.
Low in added sugars and salt, easy to fit into a controlled plan.
coach.nutrition.considerations.empty_cal: Low nutrient density: energy with little satiety.
Calorie contribution with little fiber, protein or micronutrients.
A low-satiety energy profile; better paired with more nutritious foods.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_satur: Low in saturated fat, with a lighter fat profile.
Reduced saturated fat, suitable for a leaner pattern.
A contained saturated fraction, easy to include in a balanced plan.
coach.nutrition.considerations.low_sugar: Low in simple sugars, with a more contained glucose impact.
Reduced sugar content, useful for a steadier intake.
Little simple sugar in the serving.
coach.nutrition.considerations.balanced_: A nutritionally balanced plate with a suitable macro split.
Keeps a balanced distribution of carbs, protein and fat.
Macro profile aligned with a complete, balanced plate.
coach.nutrition.considerations.dominant_: More than half of the energy comes from fat.
A fat-dominant plate; adjust the portion to the day's goal.
Macro imbalance: a high share of calories from fat.
coach.nutrition.considerations.vegetable: A relevant vegetable base with antioxidants and micronutrients.
Includes a notable contribution of vegetables and micronutrients.
Vegetable content that adds volume, fiber and micronutrients.

coach.routine.advancedTechnique.topSet.d:
Your main heavy set for the day. After warm-up, perform one top set at the heaviest load you can handle for the target rep range with solid technique.

e.g. On bench press, after build-up sets, your heaviest set of 5 reps at 100 kg.
coach.routine.advancedTechnique.backOffS:
Sets done after the top set, usually 10–20% lighter, to add volume with more controlled fatigue.

e.g. If your top set was 100 kg, next sets at 85 kg for 8–10 reps.
coach.routine.advancedTechnique.clusterS:
Split one set into mini-bunches with very short rests (10–30 s) between them so you can handle heavier weight for more total reps than in one straight set.

e.g. Instead of 6 straight squats: 2, rest 15 s, 2, rest 15 s, 2.
Maximize fibre recruitment quickly: an initial set near failure, 10–15 s rest, then mini-sets of a few reps at the same weight until you miss the target reps.

e.g. 15 leg extensions, rest 10 s, then 3s until you only get 2.
Push past initial failure: work to failure, immediately reduce load (often 20–30%) and continue for more reps.

e.g. Curl 20 kg to failure, switch to 14 kg and keep repping.
